hook: SCP-2557 does not read like a Foundation file at all. It reads like a sales page, complete with testimonials and a sign-up form, from a company claiming to have bought the entry itself. Enjoy it as satire, and pay attention to the small print.
whyItMatters: Plenty of meta entries bend the report format; this one replaces the report entirely with an advertisement. Its premise, that abstract concepts can be owned and traded, lets it treat the Foundation database as just another asset on someone's books. It is a compact example of how a parody of corporate language can carry a genuinely unsettling idea.
thingsToNotice: The testimonials escalate from odd to uncomfortable, treating real-world outcomes like stocks, before the last one dissolves into word salad. The form's dropdown menus quietly widen the setting with other universes and payment methods no ordinary bank would accept. Note that the entry changed hands because someone inside the Foundation sold it, which is the actual breach hiding behind the joke. The coupon code addressed to staff and the string at the bottom make the page feel like it is still trying to sell to you.

related.note: Another meta entry where the Foundation database itself is where things go wrong.
A short file about the Foundation's own knowledge being quietly compromised.
